channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Two Detained in Osh Region for Extortion and Threats
item.description: Two individuals were apprehended in Kyrgyzstan's Osh region for allegedly threatening a resident with online video publication and demanding money. The suspects, born in 2003 and 2007, were caught while receiving a portion of the demanded sum. A criminal case for extortion has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Replace Paper Textbooks with Tablets in Five Years
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to transition to electronic textbooks within five to six years, according to President Sadyr Japarov. The initiative aims to alleviate the burden of heavy backpacks on students. While tablet procurement is costly, they are expected to have a longer lifespan than traditional books.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Citizens Emigrating Abroad for Permanent Residence
item.description: Kazakhstan has revised the procedures for citizens wishing to move abroad for permanent residence. The Ministry of Internal Affairs has introduced new requirements for document submission and application processes, including grounds for service refusal. These updated regulations apply to Kazakh citizens, foreigners residing permanently in Kazakhstan, and stateless individuals. Applications can be submitted online via the eGov portal.

item.title: US Stock Market Plunges Over $3 Trillion After Democrats' Gains, AI Bubble Fears Grow
item.description: The US stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping 5.5% and market capitalization reducing by $2.5 trillion. The PHLX Semiconductor index fell 12.25%, the largest drop since the pandemic. The S&P 500 decreased by 4.4%, marking its worst day since April 2025. Total market value for companies in the S&P Composite 1500 fell by $3.2 trillion.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Holds Meetings in Astana on Regional Security
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a series of meetings and discussions in Astana. Discussions focused on international and regional security, the fight against terrorism and extremism within the Aqaba process framework, and new threats associated with the development of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Armenia Discuss Connecting Middle Corridor with Trump Route
item.description: Kazakhstan and Armenia explored linking the Middle Corridor transport route with the TRIPP (Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity). This potential new route through Armenia aims to provide more delivery options for carriers and attract additional cargo. The discussion occurred during a visit by Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport.

item.title: US Unveils Broader European Security Plan Ahead of Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: The White House announced a European security framework for Ukraine, including security assurances, ahead of trilateral peace talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi. The proposal, detailed by Jared Kushner, emphasizes respect for sovereignty, crisis communication, and military transparency, while NATO remains central to European defense.

item.title: Bishkek Faces School Capacity Shortage Amidst Internal and External Migration
item.description: Bishkek is experiencing a shortage of school places due to a significant influx of 12,500 students from regions and abroad. Internal migration and the return of Kyrgyz citizens from foreign countries are straining the capital's educational institutions. The Ministry of Education states that approximately 50 more schools are needed, as current construction rates cannot keep pace with the growing student population.

item.title: Central Asian Special Representatives Discuss Cooperation with Afghanistan in Bishkek
item.description: Special representatives from Central Asian countries met in Bishkek to discuss cooperation with Afghanistan. Delegations from Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan exchanged views on the political, economic, and humanitarian situation in Afghanistan and its regional impact.

item.title: Sirajuddin Haqqani Attends Graduation Ceremony for Over 400 Students in Ghazni
item.description: Afghanistan's Interior Affairs Ministry reported that Sirajuddin Haqqani attended a graduation ceremony for more than 400 students at the Noor-ul-Madaris Madrasa in Ghazni province. Graduates received certificates, and Haqqani emphasized the importance of education and religious scholarship.

item.title: Bolat Utemuratov Acquires OLX Kazakhstan for $81 Million
item.description: Bolat Utemuratov has purchased OLX Kazakhstan for $81 million through Beeline Kazakhstan. The deal gives the new owner full control of the popular classifieds platform. Utemuratov stated the investment aims to develop digital service infrastructure. OLX Kazakhstan currently has approximately 9 million active users monthly.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Sees Off Uzbek President Mirziyoyev at Astana Airport
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev bid farewell to Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the Astana airport. Mirziyoyev was in Kazakhstan for a working visit to attend the Aqaba Process summit. The summit brought together leaders from Kazakhstan, Jordan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Kyrgyzstan to discuss counter-terrorism efforts.

item.title: Activists Refuse Treatment, Election Candidates Complain, Leaders Meet in Astana
item.description: An activist hospitalized under guard refused hemodialysis. More candidates are complaining about being denied registration for local council elections. Meanwhile, a king and presidents met in Astana for the Aqaba Process summit, an international initiative against terrorism and violent extremism launched in 2015.

item.title: Almaty Police Investigate Stalking Case After Woman Reports Threats
item.description: Almaty police are investigating a stalking case after a woman reported being harassed by her ex-boyfriend. The man allegedly made threatening calls from hidden numbers and appeared at her home and workplace. He has been detained, and a criminal case has been opened.

item.title: New Railway Line Completed in Shymkent's Industrial Zone
item.description: A new 6.4-kilometer railway line has been completed in Shymkent's 'Zhuldyz' industrial zone to serve industrial enterprises. The project aligns with national goals to develop transport and logistics infrastructure, facilitating the delivery of raw materials and finished products.

item.title: Waste Incineration Plants to be Built in Almaty, Astana, and Shymkent
item.description: Waste incineration plants are planned for construction in Almaty, Astana, and Shymkent by the end of the year. A deal worth 293 billion tenge has been signed with Chinese investors. The Vice Minister of Ecology stated that the technologies will comply with European standards for emissions and quality.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Strengthen Cultural Cooperation at Symposium
item.description: An international symposium titled "Uzbekistan-Oman: Cultural Ties. Maverannahr – the Brilliance of Islamic Civilization, Spread Through Centuries" was held in Muscat. The event, part of Uzbekistan's initiative to promote Islamic heritage, showcased over 150 exhibits and discussed future cooperation in Islamic civilization studies.

item.title: Russia Increases Migrant Deportations by 50 Percent
item.description: Russia has increased migrant deportations by 50 percent, with 63,500 foreign citizens forcibly expelled in the first nine months of 2026. The number of entry bans for migrants has also risen significantly. New legislation has expanded the list of offenses leading to deportation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry of Defense Addresses Military Housing and Social Needs
item.description: The Ministry of Defense of Uzbekistan received approximately 2,500 applications in nine months, a 25% decrease from the previous year. 1,203 applications were granted, 1,130 received legal clarification, and 72 are pending. 900 military personnel were provided with mortgage housing, and 810 were relocated.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Host Rotating Symposia on Al-Farabi and Yassaui Legacies
item.description: Kazakhstan will regularly host international symposia dedicated to the legacies of thinkers Al-Farabi and Yassaui. Symposia on Al-Farabi will be held in Almaty, while those on Yassaui will take place in Turkestan. These events will alternate every two years, aiming to systematically study and promote Kazakhstan's historical and spiritual heritage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Citizens to Verify Employer Social Contribution Payments
item.description: Kazakhstan citizens can now independently verify if their employers are making timely mandatory social contributions. The Ministry of Labor explained the verification process and where to seek recourse if obligations are not met. These contributions directly impact social benefit calculations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Hosts First SCO Plus Security Dialogue in Samarkand
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service chief, Lt. Gen. Bakhodir Kurbanov, addressed the first SCO Plus Security Dialogue in Samarkand. He highlighted the exploitation of digital technologies by terrorist and extremist groups for recruitment and attacks, noting a 14% increase in identified extremist internet resources in 2026 compared to 2025. Uzbekistan's counter-terrorism efforts were recognized in the 2026 Global Terrorism Index, where it ranked 96th.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Digital Justice System to Enhance Citizen Rights Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has decreed the 'Justice-2030' strategy, aiming to build a people-centered and fair judicial system. Key reforms include the widespread adoption of digital justice, with plans to fully digitize court proceedings and implement AI technologies. The my.sud.uz portal will be updated, and over 50% of appeals will be processed electronically, making judicial procedures more accessible and efficient.

item.title: Aktobe City Administration Cancels Rally for Social Rights of People with Disabilities
item.description: The Aktobe city administration has revoked its decision to permit a rally advocating for the social rights of people with disabilities, originally scheduled for December 3. The cancellation cites emergency repair works by 'Aqtobe su-energy group' as the reason. The administration could not offer an alternative date or location due to pre-planned events.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Departs Astana After AI Security Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev concluded his working visit to Kazakhstan, where he attended the Aqaba Process summit on artificial intelligence security. He was seen off at Astana airport by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The summit focused on preventing the use of AI for terrorism.

item.title: Analysis Questions Tokayev's Choice of 'Compatriots' in National Address
item.description: An analysis of Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's recent address to the nation questions his use of the term 'compatriots.' The article argues this term is not synonymous with 'people of Kazakhstan' or 'Kazakhstanis,' citing Wikipedia and Russian legislation to define 'compatriots.'

item.title: SCO Plus Security Dialogue on Security Issues Held in Samarkand
item.description: The first expert SCO Plus Dialogue on Security Issues commenced in Samarkand on November 6, 2026, with participation from heads of special services of SCO member states, observers, and dialogue partners. The event addressed geopolitical tensions and new forms of destructive influence, including cyber threats and disinformation.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Prosecutors Secure More Accessible Transport for Disabled Residents
item.description: East Kazakhstan prosecutors have addressed a shortage of specialized transport for people with disabilities in the Ulan district. Following an inspection, it was found that only one specialized vehicle served 1,049 individuals with disabilities, with only seven using it regularly. Prosecutors intervened, leading to the allocation of two additional 'invataxi' vehicles and disciplinary action against officials.

item.title: Tashkent Metro Implements Fare Payment System Using Palm Scans
item.description: HUMO, Octobank, and UZINFOCOM have launched a new fare payment system in the Tashkent Metro that allows passengers to pay using palm scans. This innovative technology aims to streamline the payment process for commuters.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Company Director Sentenced to Six Years for Wheat Fraud and Debt
item.description: A director of 'Eclipse Agro' in Kazakhstan has been sentenced to six years in prison. He was found guilty of selling 352 tons of wheat belonging to a farming cooperative without consent and failing to pay transport services totaling 11.1 million tenge. The court also prohibited him from holding certain positions for six years.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Consul General in New York Appointed Head of Foreign Ministry's Investment Committee
item.description: The Consul General of Kazakhstan in New York has been appointed to lead the Investment Committee of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan. This appointment signifies a shift in leadership for a key department focused on attracting foreign investment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Protests Russian Army Recruitment of Citizen, Demands Return
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's embassy in Russia has sent a note to the Russian Foreign Ministry demanding the return of a citizen allegedly tricked into joining the Russian army. The citizen, identified as E.T., was reportedly recruited for a job in Russia but was sent to a military unit instead. Kyrgyzstan seeks a thorough investigation and prosecution of those responsible.

item.title: Land with Pond and Cemetery Returned to State in Almaty Region's Uigur District
item.description: The Almaty Region Prosecutor's Office has successfully reclaimed a 29.1-hectare land plot in the Uigur district, which included a pond and a cemetery, from private ownership. The land was transferred to private hands in 2008, restricting local residents' access to grazing and water resources. The court ruled to return the land to state ownership.

item.title: Azerbaijan Embassy in Tajikistan hosts Victory Day commemoration event
item.description: The Azerbaijani Embassy in Tajikistan held a ceremony to mark Victory Day, celebrated on November 8 to commemorate the 2020 Second Karabakh War victory. The event included a moment of silence for fallen soldiers and a video presentation. The Ambassador highlighted the significance of the liberation of Shusha.

item.title: Obstacles to Uzbekistan's logistics development: rail, warehousing, and competition limits
item.description: Despite growth in transport services and international status for logistics centers, Uzbekistan's 'dry ports' lack a unified system. Infrastructure, financial, and administrative barriers hinder development. Researchers warn of lost revenue if international transport corridors are not improved, proposing seven reform directions.

item.title: Kazakhstan: East Kazakhstan Region Focuses on Development and Quality of Life
item.description: Deputies of the Kurultai and members of the People's Council of Kazakhstan visited East Kazakhstan to discuss regional development and quality of life. Key issues included social infrastructure, healthcare, education, and youth opportunities. Plans include significant investment in social infrastructure over the next three years.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Bishkek for Stealing Money from Mosque Donation Box
item.description: Police in Bishkek have arrested a suspect in connection with the theft of money from a donation box at a mosque. The incident occurred on August 29, when the box was broken into and the funds stolen. A criminal case has been initiated, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Double Uranium Production
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to double its uranium production. The country is a significant producer of the radioactive element, and this expansion is part of its broader energy strategy. Further details on the timeline and specific projects were not immediately available.

item.title: Islamabad: Deportation of Afghan Citizens from US to Pakistan Under Review
item.description: Islamabad is currently reviewing the issue of Afghan citizens being deported from the United States to Pakistan. The implications and procedures surrounding these deportations are under examination.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes SCO Cooperation Against Online Youth Recruitment
item.description: Uzbekistan advocates for enhanced cooperation among SCO intelligence services to combat terrorism, cyberattacks, and the spread of extremist ideology online. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev highlighted the growing use of cyberspace by terrorist organizations for propaganda, recruitment, and fundraising, particularly targeting youth.
